cor.text:
Product and service cost, gross profit, and gross margin were as follows ($ in thousands):

Gross profit increased by $33.8 million, or 67%, for the year ended December 31, 2024, compared to 2023. The increases in gross profit was primarily attributable to the impact of the Merger, which resulted in increased revenue.

Gross profit by segment was as follows ($ in thousands):

Gross profit in the proteomics business increased by 136% to $61.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, compared to 2023. The increase was primarily driven by the impact of the Merger, which expanded our proteomics capabilities, products and services. Genomics gross profit decreased by 7% to $22.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, compared to 2023. The year over year decrease was primarily attributable to decreased revenues in the genomics segment.

sbc.heading: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.text:
We recognize compensation costs for all stock-based awards, including stock options, restrict stock units ("RSUs"), performance stock units ("PSUs") and shares of common stock purchased under our Employee Share Purchase Plan (“ESPP”), based on the grant date fair value of the award. We recognize stock-based compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the requisite service periods for non-performance-based awards. For RSUs, fair value is measured based on the closing fair market value of our common stock on the date of grant. For PSUs with a market condition, we use a Monte Carlo simulation pricing model to incorporate the market condition effects at the grant date. The Monte Carlo pricing model requires inputs which are subjective and generally requires judgment. For PSUs with performance conditions, stock-based compensation expense is recognized over the requisite service period when the achievement of each individual performance goal becomes probable.

The fair value of options and stock purchases under ESPP on the grant date is estimated using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model, which requires the use of certain subjective assumptions, including expected term, volatility, risk-free interest rate and the fair value of

our common stock. These assumptions generally require judgment.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, gross profit decreased $2.3 million, or 5%, compared to 2024, primarily due to revenue decline.

opex.heading: Operating Expenses

costs.heading: Operating Expenses
costs.text: Operating expenses were as follows ($ in thousands):

rd.heading: Research and Development
rd.text: For the year ended December 31, 2025, R&D expense decreased $2.8 million, or 10%, compared to 2024. The reduction reflects the deferral of long-term R&D projects, which reduced material and supply costs by $2.4 million. Additionally, due to restructuring activities undertaken during 2024 and 2025, personnel-related expenses declined by $0.4 million.

sm.text: SG&A expenses consist primarily of personnel costs for our sales and marketing, business development, finance, legal, human resources, information technology and general management teams, as well as professional services, including legal and accounting services.

ga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative
ga.text: SG&A expense increased $6.8 million, or 7%, for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the prior year. The increase was primarily driven by $13.7 million in increased personnel-related costs, including $8.2 million due to increased bonus expense and labor costs and $5.5 million in additional stock-based compensation expense driven by stock option grants, a $2.0 million increase in depreciation and amortization related to fixed asset additions, and a $1.3 million increase in materials and supplies driven by software licenses and subscriptions. These increases were partially offset by a $10.5 million decrease in consulting fees primarily attributable to reduced outside consulting services and contractor expenses, and a $0.8 million decrease in travel and entertainment expense.

sga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative
sga.text: SG&A expense increased $6.8 million, or 7%, for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the prior year. These increases were partially offset by a $10.5 million decrease in consulting fees primarily attributable to reduced outside consulting services and contractor expenses, and a $0.8 million decrease in travel and entertainment expense.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: Interest expense decreased by $3.3 million, or 99%, for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to 2024. During 2024, we fully repaid our then-outstanding term loan facility, as well as the balance on convertible notes issued during 2019. As a result, we had no material debt outstanding during the year ended December 31, 2025, which resulted in negligible interest expense during 2025.

tax.text: Our effective tax rates for both periods differ from the 21% U.S. Federal statutory tax rate primarily due to valuation allowances recorded against deferred tax assets on domestic losses and the tax rate differences between the United States and foreign countries.

The decrease in cash use was due to a decrease in operating expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to 2024, resulting from the completion of restructuring activities during 2024 and 2025.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Total revenue received from customers outside the United States was $56.9 million, or 67% of our total revenue in 2025, compared to $55.6 million, or 61% of our total revenue in 2024, and $62.2 million, or 59% of our total revenue in 2023.

During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, approximately 33%, 39%, and 41%, respectively, of our product and service revenue was generated from sales to customers located outside of the United States.

Revenue from customers in the United States represented $ 28.4 million, or 33 %, of total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 , $ 35.4 million, or 39 %, of total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2024 , and $ 44.1 million, or 41 %, of total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2023.

Revenue from customers in China represented $ 10.9 million, or 13 %, of total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 , 11 % of total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2024 , and 15 % of total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2023 .

Revenue from customers in Sweden represented $ 8.6 million, or 10 % of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 , 10 % of total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2024 , and 6 % of total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2023.With the exceptions of China and Sweden, no foreign country or jurisdiction had revenue in excess of 10% of the Company's total revenue during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023.

One genomics customer accounted for 12 %, 12 %, and 10 % of the Company's total revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023 , respectively, and 7 % and 10 % of outstanding net trade receivables at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
No other customer represented more than 10% of the Company's total revenue for the fiscal years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023 .

Revenue from the Company's five largest customers represented 26 % of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025, 20 % of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024, and 24 % of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2023.

Our success will depend upon their demand for and use of our products.

We may not be able to quickly establish additional or replacement suppliers, particularly for our single source components, or assembly service providers.
We rely on shipping providers to deliver products to our customers globally.

Our business operations depend upon the continuing efforts of our management team and other skilled and experienced personnel, and if we are unable to retain them or to recruit and train new key executives, scientists, and technical support personnel, we may be unable to achieve our goals.

Our future sales will depend on a number of factors including our ability to execute with our existing team, the scope of our marketing efforts and development of our direct sales force, field application specialists, and service engineer teams.

We rely on patent protection, where appropriate and available, as well as a combination of copyright, trade secret, and trademark laws, and nondisclosure, confidentiality, and other contractual restrictions to protect our proprietary technology.

We rely on licenses in order to be able to use various proprietary technologies that are material to our business, including our core IFC, multi-layer soft lithography, and mass cytometry technologies.

Additionally, our business and product development plans anticipate and may substantially depend on future in-license agreements with additional third parties, some of which are currently in the early discussion phase.

Our ability to fund future operations and meet debt covenant requirements will depend upon our level of future revenue and operating cash flow and our ability to access additional funding through either equity offerings, divestitures, issuances of debt instruments or both.
